title: Insurance Ombudsman: 1-year time limit
text: You can complain to the Insurance Ombudsman within one year of the insurer's rejection of your complaint, or within one year after the one-month wait if the insurer does not reply to your complaint at all.

title: Complain to the insurer first
text: You must first complain to the insurer's grievance cell. You can go to the Ombudsman if the insurer does not reply within one month, or if you are not satisfied with its reply.

title: Ombudsman: free, up to Rs. 50 lakh, award in 3 months
text: The Ombudsman handles complaints where the compensation does not exceed Rs. 50 lakh. No fee is payable. An award is made within 3 months of receiving all required documents (mediation recommendation within 1 month if both sides agree to mediate).

title: Documents the Ombudsman asks for
text: (a) copy of your representation to the insurer; (b) KYC such as passport or driving licence; (c) photograph (online registration); (d) insurer's letter rejecting your representation or repudiating the claim; (e) copy of the policy; (f) any other relevant documents. File online at cioins.co.in under 'Register complaint'.

title: Escalate to IRDAI (Bima Bharosa)
text: If the insurer does not respond or you are unhappy with its reply, register a complaint with IRDAI: portal bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in, email complaints@irdai.gov.in, toll-free 155255 or 1800 4254 732. Only the insured or the claimant can file; complaints by agents or other third parties are not entertained.

title: Rejection needs committee approval and stated terms
text: Under the IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (2024), para 17, a claim cannot be repudiated without approval of the insurer's Product Management Committee or Claims Review Committee, and details of a rejection or partial disallowance must be conveyed to the claimant with reference to the specific policy terms.
source_name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, 29 May 2024

title: 60-month moratorium
text: Under the IRDAI Master Circular (2024), para 13, after 60 months of continuous coverage the policy and claims cannot be contested on grounds of non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except for established fraud. Coverage credited from ported or migrated policies counts toward the 60 months.
source_name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, 29 May 2024

title: Waiting-period credits carry over
text: Under the IRDAI Master Circular (2024), accrued waiting-period credits must carry over when you renew, migrate or port a policy. Ask the insurer whether your earlier continuous cover was counted.
source_name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, 29 May 2024

title: Pre-existing disease waiting period: maximum 3 years
text: IRDAI reduced the maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases from 4 years to 3 years in 2024. Your policy schedule states the waiting period that applies to you. Verify against the current IRDAI circular before relying on this.
source_name: Business Today report on the IRDAI change (verify on irdai.gov.in)

title: Grace period for premium
text: Under the IRDAI Master Circular (2024), para 8, the grace period is 15 days for monthly instalments and 30 days for quarterly, half-yearly or annual premiums. If you renew within the grace period, accrued waiting-period credits are protected.
source_name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, 29 May 2024

title: Cashless timelines
text: Under the IRDAI Master Circular (2024), paras 15-16, for a cashless request the insurer must decide immediately but within one hour, and give final discharge authorisation within three hours of the hospital's request. This applies only if your claim was cashless.
source_name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, 29 May 2024

title: Room-rent deduction: ask for the exact clause
text: The IRDAI Master Circular reviewed here has no room-rent rule, so the policy wording decides. Ask the insurer for the exact clause, the room-rent limit in your policy schedule, and a head-by-head calculation. Ask whether the clause really allows the deduction to be applied to charges other than the room rent.
source_name: Practical tip, not a legal rule

title: Document loops: build a dated index
text: Send every document once by a traceable channel (email with read receipt, courier, portal upload) and keep proof. Make one dated index of what was sent, when and how. Ask the insurer to list in writing exactly which documents are still missing.
source_name: Practical tip, not a legal rule

title: 'Not medically necessary': get your doctor's certificate
text: Ask your treating doctor for a signed certificate stating why admission was advised and what treatment was given. Ask the insurer for the clause and the medical opinion it relied on. Rejection needs committee approval (see IRDAI-REPUD).
source_name: Practical tip, not a legal rule

title: Exclusions: read the exact clause against your records
text: Ask for the exact exclusion clause and the page of the policy where it appears. Compare its wording with your medical records. Exclusions are read narrowly: check whether your treatment truly falls inside the words used.
source_name: Practical tip, not a legal rule

title: Policy cancelled after a claim: ask for the notice and basis
text: Ask for the written cancellation notice, the evidence relied on, and the approval for cancellation. Check how many months of continuous cover you have (see IRDAI-MORATORIUM). Ask whether the premium refund was calculated correctly.
source_name: Practical tip, not a legal rule
